holds.excerpt: If test fails, engine long block replacement under extended warranty (7 years/100,000 miles).
Test neutral safety switch.
Rule out air in the cooling system and a stuck thermostat, which mimic an erratic gauge.
On the 3.0L also test the coil and ignition control module before condemning the pickup.

Pull stored fault codes via the key-on/off flash-code method to confirm a controller or driver fault, then replace the failed module (logic module, power module, SMEC, or SBEC) with a known-good or remanufactured unit and ensure clean grounds and battery voltage.
Read transmission fault codes first — limp-in is frequently a sensor (input/output speed) or wiring/voltage issue that can be fixed without a teardown;

Diagnose whether the fault is the VSS (test/replace the speed sensor on the transaxle), the speedometer cable / odometer drive gear (replace worn gear or cable on cable clusters), or the cluster itself.
The master window switch should also be tested as a potential cause.
If leak-down or compression testing shows worn piston rings or cylinder wear, the permanent fix is an engine overhaul or replacement short block/used engine, which commonly costs $2,500-$5,000+.
Recall 72B provides free diagnostic software update and battery replacement if abnormality detected.
For the 'won't read full' complaint, install the released fuel control valve kit, Mopar PN 05093967AA.
Do not judge the repair by bench-moving the sender by hand — this platform's gauge won't update that way.
Test alternator output and PCM voltage regulator function separately.
Diagnose the specific failure point: latch mechanism (Dorman 940-100), track motor, or wiring.
